prerequisites: Meeting the enrolment conditions for the Master's study programme of Mechanical Engineering - Research and Development program.

learning_outcomes.text: Have in-depth theoretical, methodological and analytical knowledge with elements of research, which is the basis for very demanding scientific and professional work in the field of synthesis, design, use, and prediction of the operation of turbine machines.
Be able to prepare complex experiments to demonstrate the characteristics and efficiency of turbine machines in power and process systems.
Be able to apply modern methods for the design and analysis of the behaviour of turbine machines under real operating conditions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction; history and importance of turbine machinery for society
Fundamentals of turbine machine operation; classification of turbine machines
The first law of thermodynamics for turbine machines; characteristic curve; efficiency; losses
Control volume approach to turbine machine analysis
Differential approach to turbine machine analysis
The fluid flow of turbine machines: Euler equation; velocity triangles; velocity, enthalpy and pressure conversion; blade shape; reactivity
Theory of similarity in turbine machines
The building blocks of hydropower systems
assessment_rules: A minimum of 80% participation in lab work is required. All lab reports must be submitted. Laboratory exams count for 50% of the grade, and other exams count for 50% of the grade.
bibliography: Marko Hočevar, Introduction to turbine machinery, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, 2019
Eck, Bruno. Fans. 1st English ed., Pergamon Press, Oxford, 1973
Dixon, S. L., Hall, C. A., Fluid Mechanics and thermodynamics of turbomachinery, Elsevier, 2010
degree: Mechanical Engineering (2nd cycle, Erasmus+ subjects, Research and Development programme)
